source.title: Circuit Fingerprints: How Answer Tokens Encode Their Geometrical Path
source.authors: A. Saurez; Neha Sengar; Dong-Soo Har

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates IOI circuit discovery using geometric attribution and compares it with gradient-based methods, rather than reproducing the original causal circuit-discovery procedure.
record.gate_note: The paper reports IOI circuit-quality metrics, a qualitative comparison of critical heads, and an IOI steering comparison. The statement that 15 heads are critical is attributed to Wang et al. (2022), not reported as a new result here, so it is not recorded as a row. Results on SVA, MCQA, emotion steering, and other non-IOI tasks are outside the claim.
record.test_reason: The paper uses IOI as a benchmark to validate a new geometric circuit-discovery and steering method. It reports its method's CPR/CMD against EAP and EAP-IG, and steering against activation patching. It never checks whether Wang et al.'s 26-head, 7-class circuit, or any listed version, holds. The head-class labels in Fig. 4 are taken from Wang et al. rather than re-established. The Fig. 2 agreement is between the authors' method and EAP-IG, not with the original circuit.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that answer-token geometry recovers circuit structure comparable to gradient-based methods: close to EAP and behind EAP-IG-inputs, a gap they attribute to simplifications in their method. They also conclude that the same directions enable steering, with an effect slightly weaker than activation patching. They do not draw conclusions about the original IOI circuit itself.
record.recipe_differences: The study scores component and edge contributions through geometric alignment with answer-token directions, and evaluates circuit quality using integrated CPR and CMD. It compares with EAP and EAP-IG-inputs but does not reproduce the original causal circuit-discovery procedure.

fits_no_version.finding: A Shapley Q/K/V decomposition at the final token (Fig. 4) shows name-mover heads as Q-dominated and S-inhibition heads as K-dominated. Head classes are taken from Wang et al. The sign grouping in the text puts duplicate-token and previous-token heads among 'negative' heads, which is odd.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: IOI head classes differ in which attention channel (query, key or value) carries their task contribution.

fits_no_version.finding: On one IOI prompt, the geometric scores and EAP-IG-inputs highlight the same heads in layers 9–11, strongest at the final token (Fig. 2). This is qualitative only.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient-free geometric attribution agrees with gradient attribution on which late-layer heads matter for IOI.

record.problems: The reported IOI tests do not ablate everything outside a 26-head circuit or verify the original 7 head classes against the stated faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria. The authors also state that their algorithm focuses on the final token position and ignores indirect effects from earlier positions and LayerNorm nonlinearities.
record.rows_left_out: Did not extract SVA and MCQA metrics in Table 1 or the non-IOI steering results because they do not bear directly on the IOI claim. Appendix Figures 7–9 show circuit diagrams for multiple models, but the paper provides no textual, numeric account of named head classes and roles in those diagrams.

untested.parts: The 26 heads, the 7 classes, and the faithfulness, completeness and minimality of the original circuit are not evaluated.
No name-mover ablation or backup-head analysis is reported.
IOI circuits are drawn for Qwen, Llama and OPT (Figs. 3 and 7), but head classes and roles are not identified or compared.
There is no comparison of any method's output with the original circuit. Ablation types and metrics are not varied.
There is no sensitivity analysis across ablations, metrics or prompt distributions.
No name-order, template or more-name variants are tested.

record.verdict_notes: This is a method paper. All rows are own-method or comparator performance and are relinked to 'none'. The reader's V1 and V4 labels are removed. The 15-critical-heads statement is cited from Wang et al., and the reader correctly excluded it. Table 1 contains apparent typos (CPR 1.50; values of 94.0 and 95.0).

versions.untested_parts: Does not establish that the original 26 attention heads in 7 classes meet faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria; it reports geometric IOI circuit scores and a comparison of critical heads.
No ablation of main name-mover heads or test of backup-head self-repair is reported.

Although IOI tracing is shown across model families, the paper does not report that the same named head classes and roles carry IOI in those models, nor that IOI components are reused for other tasks.
The paper compares its geometric method with EAP-IG-inputs for critical heads in GPT2-Small; it does not systematically compare ablation types or multiple metrics for recovery of the same circuit.
No systematic sensitivity analysis of circuit faithfulness or completeness across ablation types, metrics, or prompt distributions is reported.
No systematic test across name orders, templates, or prompts with more names is reported.
